post_text:
New York spends $26,571 per student.
Utah spends $8,154.
Utah has higher reading scores.

Explain that.

AI ranked all 50 states by NAEP 4th grade reading proficiency per $10,000 spent. The result is a 3.6× efficiency gap — and it runs the wrong direction for every state that assumes spending is the answer.

Eight of the ten highest-spending states land in the bottom half of the efficiency ranking. Washington D.C. spends $22,759 per student and finishes dead last, rank 51 of 51.

Tennessee? Ranked 16th nationally. $11,200 per pupil — $3,100 below the national average — and in the top third on outcomes per dollar. The states at the top share a thread: structured literacy mandates, K–3 reading coaches, early-grade intervention. None of those require record budgets.
